questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: Mia wants to find out how her town looked in 1950. Which of these is a primary source?
choices: A history textbook printed in 2022
A website that sums up the town's history
A photograph taken in the main street in 1950
A documentary made in 2015
questions.explanation: A primary source was made at the time, by someone who was there. The 1950 photograph is the only one made then.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: Sam asks 24 classmates how they get to school. He wants to compare how many children use each way. What is the best way to organise his answers?
choices: Write all the answers in one long paragraph
Make a tally chart with one row for each way of travelling
List the classmates in alphabetical order
Draw a map of the school grounds
questions.explanation: A tally chart puts each way of travelling in its own row, so the counts are easy to compare.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: Jack interviews his grandfather about moving to Australia in 1965. What kind of source is this interview?
choices: A secondary source, because it is spoken and not written
A secondary source, because Jack is not old enough to remember 1965
Not a source, because memories can change over time
A primary source, because his grandfather was there and saw it himself
questions.explanation: Someone who took part in an event and tells about it gives a primary source. Jack should still check details with other sources.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: A local pool counted its visitors. December: 820. January: 910. February: 870. June: 150. July: 120. August: 160. What pattern does this show?
choices: Visitor numbers stay about the same all year
Many more people visit in the summer months than in winter
Visitor numbers go up every single month
More people visit in winter than in summer
questions.explanation: December to February is summer in Australia, and those months have far more visitors than June to August.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: A town library counted the books borrowed each year. 2021: 400. 2022: 450. 2023: 500. 2024: 550. If the trend continues, how many books will be borrowed in 2025?
questions.explanation: The number goes up by 50 each year. 550 + 50 = 600.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: Lena asks three of her friends which sport they like best. All three say netball. She says, "Everyone at our school loves netball." Why is her conclusion weak?
choices: Netball is not a popular sport in Australia
Friends always tell lies in surveys
She asked only three people, so there is not enough evidence about the whole school
She should have asked only the teachers
questions.explanation: Three friends are too few to speak for a whole school. A good conclusion needs evidence from many different people.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: A mining company hands out a brochure saying its new mine will be wonderful for the town. Why should you be careful with this source?
choices: The company wants people to support the mine, so it may leave out problems
Brochures are never printed with true facts
The company is too large to know about the town
Only sources written by children can be trusted
questions.explanation: The purpose of the brochure is to persuade people. A source made to persuade may show only one side.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: Priya needs the date her town was founded. Which source is the most reliable?
choices: An unsigned post on a social media page
A history by a named historian, with a list of the records used
An advertisement for a local shop
What one neighbour thinks she remembers
questions.explanation: A named expert who lists the records used can be checked. The other sources have no clear author or no proof.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: A letter written by one settler in the 1850s shows only that person's point of view.
questions.explanation: A letter tells what one person saw and thought. Other people at the time, such as First Nations people, may have seen things differently.

questions.subject: hass
questions.prompt: Ben surveyed 30 students about how they travel to school. Bus: 17. Walk: 8. Bike: 5. Which conclusion is best supported by this evidence?
choices: Most students ride a bike
Walking is the most popular way
Nobody in the school travels by car
The bus is the most common way these students travel
questions.explanation: The bus has the biggest number, 17 out of 30. The other choices do not match the numbers.
